body_markdown:
# Introduction

A strong vocabulary begins with words you meet every day. You do not need to learn hundreds of difficult words at once. Start with useful words, understand how they work in a sentence and use them repeatedly.

The following 100 words are grouped by theme. Some words can have more than one meaning; the example shows one common use.

## 1. People and relationships

1. person — One person is waiting.
2. people — Many people work here.
3. family — My family lives nearby.
4. friend — She is my friend.
5. child — The child is reading.
6. parent — A parent cares for a child.
7. teacher — The teacher explains the lesson.
8. student — The student asks a question.
9. neighbour — Our neighbour is helpful.
10. customer — The customer needs assistance.

## 2. Common action words

11. go — I go to work.
12. come — Please come inside.
13. make — We make tea.
14. take — Take your bag.
15. give — Give me a minute.
16. get — I get up early.
17. see — I can see the bus.
18. look — Look at this picture.
19. know — I know the answer.
20. think — I think it is useful.
21. want — I want some water.
22. need — We need more time.
23. use — Use this pen.
24. work — They work together.
25. help — Please help me.
26. ask — Ask your teacher.
27. tell — Tell me the truth.
28. call — Call me later.
29. try — Try once more.
30. learn — I learn English daily.

## 3. Everyday things

31. house — Their house is small.
32. room — The room is clean.
33. door — Close the door.
34. window — Open the window.
35. water — Drink enough water.
36. food — The food is ready.
37. book — This book is useful.
38. phone — My phone is charging.
39. bag — Keep the bag here.
40. money — Save your money.

## 4. Time and frequency

41. time — What time is it?
42. day — Have a good day.
43. night — It is a quiet night.
44. morning — I walk in the morning.
45. today — I am busy today.
46. tomorrow — We will meet tomorrow.
47. yesterday — I called yesterday.
48. early — She arrives early.
49. late — The bus is late.
50. always — He always smiles.

## 5. Useful describing words

51. good — This is a good idea.
52. bad — That is bad news.
53. big — It is a big building.
54. small — I need a small box.
55. new — I bought a new book.
56. old — This is an old photo.
57. easy — The question is easy.
58. difficult — This word is difficult.
59. happy — I am happy today.
60. important — Safety is important.
61. ready — The report is ready.
62. busy — She is busy now.
63. clean — Keep your desk clean.
64. safe — The area is safe.
65. different — We have different ideas.

## 6. Places and movement

66. home — I am going home.
67. school — The school is nearby.
68. office — He works in an office.
69. hospital — The patient is in hospital.
70. market — We went to the market.
71. road — Cross the road carefully.
72. station — Meet me at the station.
73. here — Please wait here.
74. there — Put it there.
75. outside — The bus is outside.

## 7. Connecting and question words

76. and — Ravi and Neha are friends.
77. but — I am tired, but I can help.
78. because — I stayed home because it rained.
79. if — Call me if you need help.
80. with — Come with me.
81. for — This gift is for you.
82. from — I am from India.
83. before — Wash your hands before eating.
84. after — We talked after work.
85. about — Tell me about your day.
86. what — What is your name?
87. where — Where do you live?
88. when — When will you arrive?
89. why — Why are you late?
90. how — How are you?

## 8. Helpful everyday words

91. yes — Yes, I understand.
92. no — No, thank you.
93. please — Please sit down.
94. thanks — Thanks for your help.
95. sorry — Sorry, I am late.
96. very — It is very useful.
97. more — I need more practice.
98. much — How much does it cost?
99. only — I have only one question.
100. again — Please say it again.

## How to remember these words

Do not memorise all 100 in one sitting. Learn 10 words a day. For each word:
1. Read it aloud.
2. Understand the example.
3. Make one sentence about your own life.
4. Revise yesterday's words.
5. Use at least three words in a short conversation.

## Practice

Fill in the blanks using: *ready, market, because, help, tomorrow*.

1. I will visit you ___.
2. The food is ___.
3. We went to the ___ to buy vegetables.
4. I stayed home ___ I was unwell.
5. Can you ___ me?

**Answers:** 1. tomorrow, 2. ready, 3. market, 4. because, 5. help.

## Speaking challenge

Choose five words from the list and speak for one minute. Example: “I go to work in the morning. My office is near the road. I meet people and help customers. I learn English every day.”

The goal is not to use difficult vocabulary. The goal is to use familiar words correctly and confidently.

faq.question: How many words should a beginner learn daily?
faq.answer: Start with five to ten useful words and revise them regularly. Consistent use is more important than memorising a large list.

faq.question: Should I learn meanings or example sentences?
faq.answer: Learn both. Example sentences show how a word is used naturally.

faq.question: How can I remember common English words?
faq.answer: Use each word in a sentence about your daily life, speak it aloud and revise it after a day and again after a week.
